To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the EPT method based on the integral representations is less sensitive to measurement noise, that it is computationally efficient, that it can be used to reconstruct 3D profiles of conductivity and permittivity and that the reconstruction is robust to noise.

(a) the contrast source method can be used to obtain EPT reconstructions in 2D and 3D; (b) the 2D reconstructions can be used for EPT in the midplane, and the 3D reconstruc- tions can be used for 3D EPT.

(i) EPT field representations are a valid and efficient way to perform EPT, (ii) the method can easily be extended from the 2D case to the 3D case, (iii) the method is robust against noise, and (iv) the method can be used to reconstruct the dielectric profile in a loaded birdcaged coil.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of an EPT methodology based on the use of integral representations for the electromagnetic fields, which are more robust against noise and can handle inhomogeneous tissue profiles in a straightforward manner.

the development of a novel tomographic imaging modality, Electrical Properties Tomography, which is based on the reconstruction of the complex conductivity distribution from measured radio frequency (RF) fields.

the development of an EPT method based on integral (i.e., Green's tensor) representations, which is computationally efficient, robust against noise, and can easily incorporate inhomogeneous tissue profiles in the EPT reconstruction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
EPT is a viable technique for the reconstruction of inhomogeneous tissue profiles, and that the integral representation approach is a very promising technique to implement EPT.
the integral representation based EPT method has a number of attractive properties and is well suited to be used in clinical applications.
our EPT approach can be used to reconstruct tissue conductivity and permittivity distributions in a noninvasive manner with a spatial resolution in the millimeter range.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed approach is computationally very efficient and robust against noise and artifacts.
the presented EPT methodology is based on the integral representation of the electromagnetic field, is less sensitive to measurement noise and is computationally efficient.
EPT is an interesting technique to investigate the electrical properties of tissues and that it can be implemented in a practical way using integral representations of the electromagnetic field.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of contrast source inversion techniques in EPT can be a very useful tool to obtain high quality reconstructions from noisy data, especially in the presence of strong inhomogeneities.

the use of integral field representations in combination with the contrast source inversion technique provides an attractive and efficient way to reconstruct tissue conductivity profiles from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) based measurements of radio frequency fields.
the EPT reconstruction problem can be formulated in a straightforward manner using contrast source inversion (CSI) techniques.
